business_problem: Hera wanted to reduce the manual effort required to identify reusable materials at scale across its waste plants and improve recovery efficiency without disrupting complex recycling operations.
solution_summary: Hera engaged IBM Garage and IBM Consulting to design an AI-assisted waste-sorting solution that could work in real operating conditions across the company’s recycling network. The program started with on-site design thinking and operational discovery so the IBM team could understand how mixed waste moved through conveyors, how spotters identified recoverable material and where automation could realistically help. IBM then helped Hera modernize parts of its application infrastructure with IBM Cloud Paks and shape a computer-vision-based approach that analyzes waste streams, distinguishes materials such as plastics, glass, aluminum and organic matter, and feeds that intelligence into downstream sorting decisions. The architecture is intended to reduce reliance on large numbers of manual spotters while improving the amount of material that can be routed back into circular production flows.

data_flow: Operational knowledge from plant staff and plant observations informed an AI workflow that analyzes material moving on conveyors, classifies reusable waste types and feeds those signals into downstream sorting and recovery processes.
business_outcome: Hera built a path toward more efficient material recovery and reduced manual sorting effort while supporting its circular-economy goals across a very large waste-processing footprint.
